Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

Coverage and verification procedure:
Before building, record a short reference inventory in program comments: major visible
objects, their approximate normalized image bounds, distinctive visible parts, overlaps,
and uncertain or occluded regions. These are estimates from this input, not calibration.
Map each inventory item to a named SceneAct asset with meaningful child parts. A valid
hierarchy verifies only the parts you emitted; it does not establish image completeness.
Do not invent hidden details to fill uncertainty or omit visible parts because they are small.
For composite objects, match the overall silhouette and the distribution of occupied space
and gaps before adding fine repeated details. Estimate component sizes relative to their
parent and nearby objects from the reference. A correct outer bounding box alone does not
ensure the correct internal density, component proportions or visible coverage. Keep these
parameters explicit so that a later revision can change them without rebuilding the design.

Use the first execution for a complete scene, leaving the second available for correction.
After a successful render, compare the reference inventory against the full rendered view:
missing or extra visible parts, silhouette, internal gaps, relative sizes, overlaps and image
bounds. Identify the largest supported discrepancies before revising. If many objects share
a displacement or scale error, consider camera/framing; if a discrepancy is local, consider
that object's parameters. Neither pattern proves a unique cause. Preserve matching objects
and their editable hierarchy while correcting the supported discrepancies. Do not impose
one fixed density, camera, object count or parameter adjustment across different inputs.
An isolated-object view, if supplied, can clarify membership and silhouette, but its full-image
score is not evidence that removing the rest of the scene improves the reconstruction.
Keep unresolved mappings and occluded geometry explicitly uncertain.

Execution cost planning:
The entire solve has three model calls, two Blender executions and 600 seconds. A short
Python loop can generate thousands of Blender objects before any image exists. Plan a
compact complete first build so that realization and the runner's render can finish with
time for review. Do not change the runner's resource policy or rendering settings to evade
this budget. Use geometry complexity as the controllable cost.
Before returning code, estimate expanded primitive counts in comments, including nested
loops and helper calls. In this implementation, each ball, rod and box emits a separate
mesh and marker; a fillet_box can expand to 26 primitives; sweep_tube with n points emits
2*n-1 primitives. Cloning and layout helpers duplicate their contents. Boolean operands
also incur mesh creation and modifier work. Count these expansions, not just named assets.
Aim initially for a few hundred primitive meshes across the whole scene, as a planning
heuristic rather than a measured runtime guarantee or fixed object count. Allocate detail
according to visible pixel size, silhouette and gaps. If the estimate reaches thousands,
simplify repeated microstructure before execution while retaining every inventory object
and its meaningful editable parts. Represent unresolved surface detail with shared materials
and restrained procedural shading; retain geometric detail that changes visible contours,
openings or occlusions. Avoid nested per-element decoration below the image resolution.
Use short, adaptively spaced tube paths for visible curves, concentrating points at bends.
Avoid many nearly identical Boolean slices to approximate one hollow shape; use a small
number of appropriate SceneAct solids and cutters, preserving the visible opening. Prefer
boxes or scaled balls where their silhouettes suffice; reserve fillet_box for parts whose
rounded edges matter. Keep a small reusable material palette for each surface family rather
than generating a distinct random color and material for every tiny primitive. Keep parent
assets, semantic child parts, and support relations intact during simplification.
If execution times out without an image, report that completion failed and the bottleneck
is unknown unless logs locate it. When a retry remains, reduce expanded primitive counts,
Boolean operations and material proliferation in the complete program. Do not infer camera,
coverage or appearance defects from a timeout. A reduced-cost build still needs execution
and rendered-image verification; simplification alone is not evidence of success.

Execution verification:
realize(scene) clears Blender to an empty factory scene. Configure the world, camera,
lighting and materials after realization; do not assume a default world exists. When setting
world nodes, use this initialization after realize:
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    if sc.world is None:
        sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('SceneWorld')
    sc.world.use_nodes = True
    background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('Background')
    if background is None:
        background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBackground')
    output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('World Output')
    if output is None:
        output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputWorld')
    sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs['Background'], output.inputs['Surface'])
Before returning code, check API arguments, positive dimensions, noncoincident rod endpoints,
and fillet radii against the smallest dimension. If execution fails, use the actual traceback
to repair the program. A failed execution without an image supplies no rendered visual
feedback: do not treat it as evidence for unrelated camera or geometry changes. Preserve
explicit failures and unknowns; do not claim verification when no successful render exists.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)

```python
from sceneact import *
import bpy, math, random
from mathutils import Vector

# Reference inventory (normalized image bounds, approximate):
# room: ceiling (0,0)-(1,.40), ivory walls, dark carpet (.0,.59)-(1,1).
# Right wall whiteboard (.59,.26)-(.92,.59): pale face, narrow aluminum
# perimeter, central seam and lower tray; near edge overlaps the wall.
# Back wall (.11,.38)-(.53,.61): dark vent, open electrical box, hanging
# cover, two small labels, black skirting.
# Ceiling: large acoustic tiles and narrow rails, missing tiles mainly
# at upper-left and above the flag; exposed dark cavities are uncertain.
# Flag (.45,.33)-(.51,.43): diagonal pole, blue canton, hanging red/white folds.
# Left wall (.0,.35)-(.12,.67): brightly lit pale panels with thin seams.
# Floor debris: dark broken panels at (.04,.63)-(.37,.72), (.05,.74)-(.41,.80);
# narrow rails (.15,.71)-(.43,.75), yellow bent panel (.56,.67)-(.90,.79),
# and long metal strips (.78,.77)-(1,.90). No furniture is visible.
# Named assets below preserve these groups. Hidden room extent is uncertain.
# Expanded estimate: architecture 16, ceiling tiles/rails/cavities 112,
# whiteboard 8, back fixtures 17, flag 23, debris 35: about 211 primitives.
# No fillets, booleans, or dense curve expansions.

random.seed(18)
scene = Scene('Abandoned classroom')
cream = (.72,.70,.63)
ceiling_color = (.68,.70,.69)
metal = (.52,.56,.55)
dark = (.065,.075,.070)
floor_color = (.105,.115,.102)

def addbox(parent, name, size, center, color, rotation=None):
    n = box(size=size, center=center, color=color)
    if rotation:
        n.turn(euler=rotation)
    parent.include(name,n)
    return n

room = Asset('room_architecture')
addbox(room,'carpet',(4.8,10.7,.10),(0,4.15,-.05),floor_color)
addbox(room,'right_ivory_wall',(.13,10.7,3.12),(2.36,4.15,1.54),cream)
addbox(room,'back_ivory_wall',(4.8,.13,3.12),(0,8.48,1.54),cream)
addbox(room,'left_bright_wall',(.12,10.7,3.12),(-2.36,4.15,1.54),(.82,.83,.79))
addbox(room,'back_black_baseboard',(4.7,.035,.13),(0,8.39,.065),dark)
addbox(room,'right_black_baseboard',(.035,10.7,.14),(2.28,4.15,.07),dark)
addbox(room,'left_black_baseboard',(.035,10.7,.11),(-2.28,4.15,.055),dark)
for y in [2.0,4.0,6.0]:
    addbox(room,'left_vertical_panel_seam_'+str(y),(.012,.014,2.9),(-2.288,y,1.5),(.66,.69,.67))
for z in [.78,1.55,2.32]:
    addbox(room,'left_horizontal_seam_'+str(z),(.012,8.0,.012),(-2.287,4.4,z),(.71,.73,.70))
scene.include('architecture',room)

ceiling = Asset('suspended_acoustic_ceiling')
addbox(ceiling,'dark_plenum',(4.8,10.7,.08),(0,4.15,3.20),(.12,.15,.14))
# Sparse missing panels expose the suspension cavities.
missing = {(0,2),(0,3),(0,5),(0,6),(1,6),(3,7)}
for ix in range(8):
    for iy in range(9):
        x=-2.1+ix*.6
        y=-1.1+iy*1.16
        if (ix,iy) in missing:
            continue
        c = .675 + random.uniform(-.025,.025)
        addbox(ceiling,f'tile_{ix}_{iy}',(.586,1.145,.035),(x,y,3.055),(c,c+.015,c+.01))
for ix in range(9):
    addbox(ceiling,f'long_rail_{ix}',(.018,10.5,.024),(-2.4+ix*.6,4.0,3.035),(.63,.67,.65))
for iy in range(10):
    addbox(ceiling,f'cross_rail_{iy}',(4.8,.018,.024),(0,-1.68+iy*1.16,3.034),(.63,.67,.65))
# Two subtly translucent rectangular ceiling light diffusers.
for k,y in enumerate([2.0,5.48]):
    addbox(ceiling,'light_frame_'+str(k),(.62,1.17,.032),(-1.2,y,3.028),(.56,.60,.59))
    addbox(ceiling,'light_diffuser_'+str(k),(.565,1.10,.015),(-1.2,y,3.005),(.78,.81,.80))
detector = ball(.075,center=(-1.25,1.8,2.995),color=(.79,.79,.73))
detector.resize((1,1,.38))
ceiling.include('smoke_detector',detector)
scene.include('ceiling',ceiling)

board = Asset('large_right_wall_whiteboard')
board_y0,board_y1 = 3.60,7.48
board_z0,board_z1 = 1.03,2.61
addbox(board,'backing',(.055,board_y1-board_y0,board_z1-board_z0),
       (2.255,(board_y0+board_y1)/2,(board_z0+board_z1)/2),(.71,.74,.72))
addbox(board,'writing_face',(.018,board_y1-board_y0-.07,board_z1-board_z0-.065),
       (2.216,(board_y0+board_y1)/2,(board_z0+board_z1)/2),(.79,.82,.82))
for name,y in [('near',board_y0),('far',board_y1)]:
    addbox(board,name+'_aluminum_upright',(.045,.027,board_z1-board_z0+.03),(2.193,y,(board_z0+board_z1)/2),metal)
for name,z in [('top',board_z1),('bottom',board_z0)]:
    addbox(board,name+'_aluminum_rail',(.045,board_y1-board_y0+.04,.027),(2.194,(board_y0+board_y1)/2,z),metal)
addbox(board,'center_division',(.021,.014,board_z1-board_z0-.04),(2.196,5.67,(board_z0+board_z1)/2),(.65,.69,.69))
addbox(board,'lower_marker_tray',(.105,board_y1-board_y0,.027),(2.17,(board_y0+board_y1)/2,1.014),(.59,.62,.60))
scene.include('whiteboard',board)

fixtures=Asset('back_wall_utilities')
addbox(fixtures,'vent_frame',(.88,.035,.41),(-1.38,8.386,1.82),(.52,.55,.52))
addbox(fixtures,'vent_dark_opening',(.79,.025,.33),(-1.38,8.36,1.82),(.23,.28,.28))
for i in range(5):
    addbox(fixtures,'vent_louver_'+str(i),(.77,.025,.012),(-1.38,8.34,1.70+i*.057),(.32,.36,.35))
addbox(fixtures,'electrical_box_rim',(.34,.045,.45),(-.23,8.37,1.55),(.54,.56,.51))
addbox(fixtures,'electrical_box_interior',(.265,.025,.37),(-.23,8.333,1.55),(.16,.19,.17))
addbox(fixtures,'electric_pale_component',(.07,.025,.20),(-.29,8.31,1.58),(.67,.68,.60))
addbox(fixtures,'electric_wire',(.025,.03,.21),(-.18,8.30,1.59),(.36,.39,.33),rotation=(0,12,0))
addbox(fixtures,'loose_hanging_metal_cover',(.48,.05,.39),(-.04,8.24,1.22),(.43,.49,.46),rotation=(0,-38,0))
for k,x in enumerate([.40,.64]):
    addbox(fixtures,'wall_label_'+str(k),(.16,.015,.20),(x,8.39,1.38),(.76,.75,.66))
    addbox(fixtures,'label_mark_'+str(k),(.095,.008,.025),(x,8.375,1.42),(.42,.44,.38))
scene.include('back_utilities',fixtures)

flag = Asset('hanging_american_flag')
flag.include('angled_flagpole',rod(.012,start=(2.24,7.67,2.66),end=(1.23,7.55,2.91),color=(.30,.31,.27)))
# The flag hangs in narrow folds: the striped field is vertically oriented.
for i in range(13):
    x=1.205+i*.034
    z=2.54 - .04*math.sin(i*.45)
    col=(.60,.075,.065) if i%2==0 else (.82,.80,.70)
    addbox(flag,'fabric_stripe_'+str(i),(.034,.018,.62),
           (x,7.53+.026*math.sin(i*1.1),z),col,rotation=(0,-5,0))
addbox(flag,'blue_canton',(.19,.024,.25),(1.30,7.505,2.75),(.13,.19,.26),rotation=(0,-5,0))
for ix in range(3):
    for iz in range(3):
        addbox(flag,f'canton_star_{ix}_{iz}',(.011,.008,.011),
               (1.24+ix*.048,7.487,2.68+iz*.062),(.81,.81,.72))
scene.include('flag',flag)

debris=Asset('fallen_ceiling_and_floor_debris')
def panel(name,x,y,sx,sy,angle,color,z=.026):
    return addbox(debris,name,(sx,sy,.025),(x,y,z),color,rotation=(0,0,angle))

# Thin broken ceiling sheets, with dark undersides and offset fragments.
panel('foreground_dark_tile',-1.11,2.36,1.48,.58,-9,(.20,.23,.21))
panel('foreground_gray_facing',-1.30,2.44,1.05,.43,-9,(.40,.42,.37),.045)
panel('foreground_right_fragment',-.68,2.57,.61,.28,16,(.32,.35,.30),.061)
panel('foreground_small_flap',-1.47,2.64,.48,.29,-26,(.49,.50,.43),.063)
panel('middle_left_dark_panel',-1.75,4.26,1.08,.48,-11,(.19,.22,.20))
panel('middle_left_light_fragment',-1.91,4.32,.69,.35,-11,(.49,.50,.43),.046)
panel('middle_panel_splinter',-1.32,4.33,.43,.19,21,(.34,.37,.32),.055)
panel('back_dark_panel',-.98,6.12,1.04,.39,15,(.16,.19,.17))
panel('back_light_fragment',-1.25,6.07,.45,.23,15,(.44,.46,.39),.046)
panel('back_small_chip',-.65,6.33,.31,.16,-20,(.35,.37,.31),.054)
# Reflective exposed ceiling strips across the carpet.
addbox(debris,'long_center_aluminum_strip',(1.54,.052,.025),(-.50,3.83,.055),(.63,.68,.67),rotation=(0,1,-12))
addbox(debris,'center_strip_dark_side',(1.5,.016,.026),(-.50,3.80,.059),(.31,.36,.34),rotation=(0,1,-12))
addbox(debris,'rear_bent_strip',(.73,.025,.02),(-.73,6.37,.065),(.48,.53,.50),rotation=(0,0,21))
for k in range(7):
    x=random.uniform(-1.9,1.95)
    y=random.uniform(2.7,7.6)
    panel('small_plaster_chip_'+str(k),x,y,random.uniform(.05,.13),random.uniform(.04,.09),random.uniform(0,180),(.49,.49,.40),.025)

# Yellow fiberglass/ceiling panel on right, with a lifted arched outer end.
yellow=(.63,.51,.19)
panel('yellow_panel_underlayer',1.30,3.03,1.40,1.13,-5,(.56,.46,.19),.055)
# Adjacent broad sections form a bent, continuous sheet silhouette.
for i,(x,z,tilt) in enumerate([(0.86,.12,-5),(1.15,.16,-9),(1.44,.23,-17),(1.72,.22,18)]):
    addbox(debris,'yellow_bent_sheet_section_'+str(i),(.33,1.14,.035),(x,3.02,z),yellow,rotation=(0,tilt,-5))
addbox(debris,'yellow_torn_front_tab',(.19,.70,.028),(.77,2.80,.085),(.68,.56,.24),rotation=(0,8,-7))
addbox(debris,'yellow_fold_crease',(.028,1.13,.025),(1.30,3.01,.205),(.48,.40,.17),rotation=(0,-9,-5))
# Two long rails extend diagonally toward the right foreground edge.
addbox(debris,'foreground_long_white_rail',(.075,2.27,.035),(1.89,1.30,.045),(.68,.69,.63),rotation=(0,0,-25))
addbox(debris,'foreground_parallel_metal_rail',(.045,1.87,.032),(2.15,1.56,.050),(.47,.52,.51),rotation=(0,0,-31))
scene.include('floor_debris',debris)

# A small outlet below the board.
outlet=Asset('right_wall_outlet')
addbox(outlet,'ivory_plate',(.016,.10,.15),(2.278,6.10,.54),(.72,.68,.55))
addbox(outlet,'socket',(.019,.028,.045),(2.265,6.10,.54),(.48,.46,.36))
scene.include('outlet',outlet)

realize(scene)

sc=bpy.context.scene
if sc.world is None:
    sc.world=bpy.data.worlds.new('SceneWorld')
sc.world.use_nodes=True
nodes=sc.world.node_tree.nodes
background=nodes.get('Background')
if background is None:
    background=nodes.new('ShaderNodeBackground')
output=nodes.get('World Output')
if output is None:
    output=nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputWorld')
sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs['Background'],output.inputs['Surface'])
background.inputs['Color'].default_value=(.66,.72,.78,1)
background.inputs['Strength'].default_value=.36

# Restrained procedural carpet and plaster detail, without image textures.
for mat in bpy.data.materials:
    mat.use_nodes=True
    bs=mat.node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
    if bs is None:
        continue
    bs.inputs['Roughness'].default_value=.86
    c=bs.inputs['Base Color'].default_value
    if abs(c[0]-floor_color[0])<.018 and abs(c[1]-floor_color[1])<.018:
        nt=mat.node_tree
        tex=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise')
        tex.inputs['Scale'].default_value=155
        tex.inputs['Detail'].default_value=2
        ramp=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position=.19
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color=(.055,.065,.057,1)
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position=.81
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color=(.19,.20,.17,1)
        nt.links.new(tex.outputs['Fac'],ramp.inputs[0])
        nt.links.new(ramp.outputs[0],bs.inputs['Base Color'])
        bump=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBump')
        bump.inputs['Strength'].default_value=.28
        bump.inputs['Distance'].default_value=.018
        nt.links.new(tex.outputs['Fac'],bump.inputs['Height'])
        nt.links.new(bump.outputs['Normal'],bs.inputs['Normal'])

set_view(position=(-1.65,-.85,1.69),target=(.25,7.1,1.52),lens=23.5,sensor=36)
area_emitter(position=(-3.5,2.7,2.15),power=750,size=4.2,target=(.5,5.0,1.0),color=(.88,.94,1.0))
area_emitter(position=(-.4,1.5,2.86),power=130,size=3.0,target=(0,5,.3),color=(1.0,.96,.87))
sc.view_settings.view_transform='Standard'
sc.view_settings.exposure=0
sc.view_settings.gamma=1
```
